<content>
1: # Pathland Design Tokens
2: 
3: **Status:** Draft
4: **Last Updated:** October 1, 2026
5: 
6: ---
7: 
8: ## Purpose
9: 
10: Design tokens are the application-facing vocabulary for **look and feel** —
11: colors, typography, spacing, radii (roundings), border widths, elevations, and
12: control styling. They let an application **roll a full theme** — including a
13: **dark variant** — that is honored consistently across every renderer, while
14: leaving platform-native defaults and interaction-state styling to the renderer.
15: 
16: This document is the companion catalog for the [Design Token
17: System](./OPCODE.md#design-token-system). It defines:
18: 
19: - the **standard token catalog** (what renderers must understand),
20: - the **resolution contract** (override → default → parent → fallback),
21: - the **color-scheme contract** (base = light, `dark.` = dark), and
22: - the **renderer integration contract** (how future native renderers adopt it).
23: 
24: The wire encoding (`PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`, the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type)
25: lives in [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md). Modifier mapping lives in
26: [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md). The DSL surface is specified in
27: [DSL.md](./DSL.md).
28: 
29: > **Implementation status** is tracked per implementing project (a `status.md`
30: > in each protocol crate/library), **not** in this specification. This document
31: > defines the protocol contract only.
32: 
33: ---
34: 
35: ## Core Principle
36: 
37: > **The application owns the theme. The renderer owns the defaults, the scheme
38: > detection, and the interaction states.**
39: 
40: - The **application** declares a theme: token overrides (base values = the
41:   **light** design, `dark.`-prefixed values = the **dark** design) and, in a
42:   style property, a **token reference** instead of a literal value.
43: - The **renderer** supplies platform-appropriate defaults for the standard
44:   catalog (both light and dark), derives the **effective color scheme** from the
45:   platform (OS / browser / native theme), resolves token references, and owns
46:   hover/pressed/focus/disabled styling.
47: 
48: This preserves native look-and-feel by default and gives the application
49: cross-renderer consistency when it overrides tokens.
50: 
51: ### Ownership
52: 
53: | Aspect | Owner |
54: |--------|-------|
55: | Theme values (base + `dark.*`) | Application |
56: | Color-scheme detection (light/dark) | Renderer (platform-derived) |
57: | Default token values (light + dark) | Renderer |
58: | Token resolution (override → default → fallback) | Renderer |
59: | Interaction states (hover/pressed/focus/disabled) | Renderer |
60: | Literal property values | Application |
61: 
62: ---
63: 
64: ## Token Identification
65: 
66: Tokens are identified by **dot-separated string paths** — `color.primary`,
67: `font.body.size`, `space.2` — case-sensitive, lowercase recommended. A `dark.`
68: prefix selects the **dark variant** of a token (`dark.color.primary`).
69: 
70: The path namespace is **open**: the standard catalog below is a contract the
71: renderer MUST implement; any path outside it is **application-defined** and
72: renderer-optional (the renderer falls back rather than erroring).
73: 
74: ---
75: 
76: ## Value Types
77: 
78: A token's value uses the standard [value types](./OPCODE.md#value-types) —
79: `COLOR` (packed `0xAARRGGBB`, sRGB), `F32`, `U32`, `I32`, `U8`, `STRING`, `ENUM`.
80: 
81: A **token reference** in a property uses the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type (`0x08`):
82: `C` = arenaRef to the token path. A property carries **exactly one** value —
83: either a literal (`COLOR`/`F32`/…) or a token reference, never both (see
84: [References in properties](#references-in-properties)).
85: 
86: ---
87: 
88: ## Standard Token Catalog
89: 
90: The catalog is layered. **Tier 1 (core)** tokens are mandatory: a renderer MUST
91: provide light and dark defaults and resolve them. **Tier 2 (extended)** tokens
92: are recommended: a renderer SHOULD provide defaults, and an application MAY
93: override them; a renderer that cannot apply a Tier 2 token ignores it (the same
94: "allowed and ignored" rule as unapplicable modifiers).
95: 
96: Default values are **renderer-owned and platform-appropriate**; the tables below
97: name the tokens and their *meaning*, never concrete values. The renderer MUST
98: resolve tokens by name and MAY map them onto native semantic resources (e.g. the
99: platform's system text color for `color.text.primary`).
100: 
101: ### Colors — Tier 1
102: 
103: | Token | Meaning |
104: |-------|---------|
105: | `color.primary` | Primary brand / accent fill |
106: | `color.secondary` | Secondary brand / accent fill |
107: | `color.background` | Document / canvas background |
108: | `color.surface` | Raised surface (cards, panels, popovers) |
109: | `color.text.primary` | Primary text color |
110: | `color.text.secondary` | Secondary / muted text color |
111: | `color.text.onPrimary` | Text placed on a `color.primary` fill |
112: | `color.border` | Default border / outline color |
113: | `color.accent` | Accent for controls (focus, selection, toggle fill) |
114: 
115: Tier 2: `color.separator` (hairline dividers), and status colors
116: `color.success`, `color.warning`, `color.danger`, `color.info`.
117: 
118: ### Typography — Tier 1 core
119: 
120: | Token | Meaning |
121: |-------|---------|
122: | `font.body.size` | Body text size |
123: | `font.body.weight` | Body text weight (100–900) |
124: | `font.body.family` | Body font family (STRING) |
125: 
126: Tier 2: `font.body.lineHeight`, `font.caption.size`,
127: `font.heading.1.size`–`font.heading.6.size` (with matching `.weight`/`.family`
128: paths), `font.mono.family`.
129: 
130: The **predefined typographies** (`TEXT_STYLE`: `LargeTitle`…`Caption2`,
131: spec/MODIFIERS.md §2) are the semantic counterparts of these token paths: the
132: renderer owns their concrete size/weight (a baked per-renderer HIG scale). An
133: application that wants full control can instead bind text to a `TEXT_STYLE` of
134: its own via the `font.<style>.*` token paths above, or set an explicit
135: `FONT_SIZE`/`FONT_WEIGHT`/`FONT_FAMILY` override on top.
136: 
137: ### Spacing — Tier 1
138: 
139: Spacing is a **generative family** (Tailwind-v4 style): one base unit
140: multiplied by an arbitrary number.
141: 
142: | Token | Meaning |
143: |-------|---------|
144: | `space.base` | The spacing **unit** (F32) — override this to change the whole density |
145: | `space.<N>` | `space.base` × N, where N is any positive decimal (`space.1`, `space.2`, `space.0.5`, `space.3.75`) — **computed** by the resolver |
146: 
147: Rules:
148: 
149: 1. The `space.<N>` family is **generative**, not independently valued: the
150:    renderer resolves `space.base` and multiplies by the numeric leaf. Individual
151:    members MUST NOT be overridden via `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` — override `space.base`
152:    to control the whole scale.
153: 2. The color-scheme layer and parent fallback apply to `space.base`, never to an
154:    individual `space.<N>` member (`dark.space.2` is not a token; the dark layer
155:    is `dark.space.base`).
156: 3. A spacing/padding property MAY carry a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference to any
157:    `space.<N>` path — e.g. a DSL expresses `.padding(space.2)` or `Space(2)`.
158:    Literal F32 spacing values remain valid and unthemed.
159: 
160: Tier 2: `size.control.xs` / `sm` / `md` / `lg` — standard control heights.
161: 
162: ### Radius (roundings) — Tier 1
163: 
164: | Token | Meaning |
165: |-------|---------|
166: | `radius.xs` / `radius.sm` / `radius.md` / `radius.lg` / `radius.xl` | Corner radius scale (F32) |
167: | `radius.full` | Fully round (pill/circle) — renderer resolves to its "infinite" value |
168: 
169: ### Borders — Tier 1 core
170: 
171: | Token | Meaning |
172: |-------|---------|
173: | `border.width.thin` | Default hairline/border width |
174: 
175: Tier 2: `border.width.thick`.
176: 
177: ### Elevation — Tier 2
178: 
179: Shadows are composite; each component is its own token:
180: 
181: | Token | Meaning |
182: |-------|---------|
183: | `elevation.low.color` / `radius` / `x` / `y` / `blur` | Low elevation shadow |
184: | `elevation.high.color` / `radius` / `x` / `y` / `blur` | High elevation shadow |
185: 
186: ### Opacity — Tier 2
187: 
188: | Token | Meaning |
189: |-------|---------|
190: | `opacity.disabled` | The renderer MAY apply this to disabled controls. The disabled **state** itself is the `ENABLED` property; its visual handling (including this opacity) remains renderer-owned. |
191: 
192: ### Shared control core — Tier 1
193: 
194: Tokens every control-style component (buttons, inputs, switches, sliders, …)
195: shares. Renderers MUST resolve these; an individual token a renderer cannot
196: apply is ignored.
197: 
198: | Token | Meaning |
199: |-------|---------|
200: | `control.background` | Control resting background |
201: | `control.foreground` | Control content (label/icon) color |
202: | `control.border` | Control border color |
203: | `control.border.width` | Control border width |
204: | `control.radius` | Control corner radius |
205: | `control.padding.horizontal` / `control.padding.vertical` | Control inner padding |
206: | `control.height` | Control height (F32) |
207: | `control.font.size` / `control.font.weight` | Control text |
208: | `control.accent` | Control accent (fill, selection, focus) |
209: 
210: ### Per-component tokens
211: 
212: Small sets; only where a component's semantics genuinely differ from
213: `control.*`. All Tier 1 unless noted.
214: 
215: **Buttons** (Tier 1): `button.background`, `button.foreground`, `button.border`,
216: `button.radius`, `button.padding`, `button.height`, `button.font.size`,
217: `button.font.weight`, `button.accent`.
218: 
219: **Text fields / editors** (Tier 1): `input.background`, `input.foreground`,
220: `input.placeholder`, `input.border`, `input.radius`, `input.font.size`.
221: 
222: **Toggle / switch** (Tier 1): `toggle.accent`, `toggle.track.off`,
223: `toggle.track.on`, `toggle.thumb`.
224: 
225: **Slider** (Tier 1): `slider.accent`, `slider.track`, `slider.thumb`.
226: 
227: **Progress / gauge** (Tier 1): `progress.track`, `progress.fill`,
228: `gauge.track`, `gauge.fill`.
229: 
230: **Stepper** (Tier 2): `stepper.accent`, `stepper.background`, `stepper.border`,
231: `stepper.radius`.
232: 
233: **Picker** (Tier 2): `picker.accent`, `picker.background`, `picker.border`,
234: `picker.radius`.
235: 
236: **Menu** (Tier 2): `menu.background`, `menu.foreground`, `menu.border`,
237: `menu.radius`.
238: 
239: **Label** (Tier 2): `label.foreground`, `label.font.size`.
240: 
241: ---
242: 
243: ## Color Schemes (Light / Dark)
244: 
245: Base token paths define the **light** design. A `dark.`-prefixed path defines
246: the **dark** design for the same token.
247: 
248: The renderer derives the **effective color scheme** from its platform's native
249: light/dark signal — it is **never** carried by the protocol.
250: 
251: ### Rules
252: 
253: 1. **Base = light.** `color.primary` is the light value; `dark.color.primary`
254:    is the dark value.
255: 2. A renderer MUST provide **both** light and dark defaults for every Tier 1
256:    token (platform-appropriate). Dark mode therefore works even when the
257:    application only overrides base tokens.
258: 3. The application rolls a full theme by overriding base values and — where the
259:    dark look must differ — `dark.*` values.
260: 4. The renderer MUST **re-resolve** every token-referencing property when the
261:    effective scheme changes, and MAY animate the transition.
262: 5. The `dark.` prefix is the first scheme prefix; the namespace is open so
263:    custom schemes could follow. Only `light` (base) and `dark` are
264:    standardized.
265: 
266: ---
267: 
268: ## Resolution
269: 
270: ```
271: FUNCTION resolveToken(tokenPath, scheme):
272:     # Walk most-specific → least-specific, applying the dark layer first.
273:     layers = []
274:     if scheme == dark:
275:         layers += [dark.path, dark.parent(path), …dark.root]   # dark.* layer
276:     layers += [path, parent(path), …root]                       # base layer
277: 
278:     for candidate in layers:

# Pathland Design Tokens

**Status:** Draft
**Last Updated:** October 1, 2026

---

## Purpose

Design tokens are the application-facing vocabulary for **look and feel** —
colors, typography, spacing, radii (roundings), border widths, elevations, and
control styling. They let an application **roll a full theme** — including a
**dark variant** — that is honored consistently across every renderer, while
leaving platform-native defaults and interaction-state styling to the renderer.

This document is the companion catalog for the [Design Token
System](./OPCODE.md#design-token-system). It defines:

- the **standard token catalog** (what renderers must understand),
- the **resolution contract** (override → default → parent → fallback),
- the **color-scheme contract** (base = light, `dark.` = dark), and
- the **renderer integration contract** (how future native renderers adopt it).

The wire encoding (`PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`, the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type)
lives in [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md). Modifier mapping lives in
[MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md). The DSL surface is specified in
[DSL.md](./DSL.md).

> **Implementation status** is tracked per implementing project (a `status.md`
> in each protocol crate/library), **not** in this specification. This document
> defines the protocol contract only.

---

## Core Principle

> **The application owns the theme. The renderer owns the defaults, the scheme
> detection, and the interaction states.**

- The **application** declares a theme: token overrides (base values = the
  **light** design, `dark.`-prefixed values = the **dark** design) and, in a
  style property, a **token reference** instead of a literal value.
- The **renderer** supplies platform-appropriate defaults for the standard
  catalog (both light and dark), derives the **effective color scheme** from the
  platform (OS / browser / native theme), resolves token references, and owns
  hover/pressed/focus/disabled styling.

This preserves native look-and-feel by default and gives the application
cross-renderer consistency when it overrides tokens.

### Ownership

| Aspect | Owner |
|--------|-------|
| Theme values (base + `dark.*`) | Application |
| Color-scheme detection (light/dark) | Renderer (platform-derived) |
| Default token values (light + dark) | Renderer |
| Token resolution (override → default → fallback) | Renderer |
| Interaction states (hover/pressed/focus/disabled) | Renderer |
| Literal property values | Application |

---

## Token Identification

Tokens are identified by **dot-separated string paths** — `color.primary`,
`font.body.size`, `space.2` — case-sensitive, lowercase recommended. A `dark.`
prefix selects the **dark variant** of a token (`dark.color.primary`).

The path namespace is **open**: the standard catalog below is a contract the
renderer MUST implement; any path outside it is **application-defined** and
renderer-optional (the renderer falls back rather than erroring).

---

## Value Types

A token's value uses the standard [value types](./OPCODE.md#value-types) —
`COLOR` (packed `0xAARRGGBB`, sRGB), `F32`, `U32`, `I32`, `U8`, `STRING`, `ENUM`.

A **token reference** in a property uses the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type (`0x08`):
`C` = arenaRef to the token path. A property carries **exactly one** value —
either a literal (`COLOR`/`F32`/…) or a token reference, never both (see
[References in properties](#references-in-properties)).

---

## Standard Token Catalog

The catalog is layered. **Tier 1 (core)** tokens are mandatory: a renderer MUST
provide light and dark defaults and resolve them. **Tier 2 (extended)** tokens
are recommended: a renderer SHOULD provide defaults, and an application MAY
override them; a renderer that cannot apply a Tier 2 token ignores it (the same
"allowed and ignored" rule as unapplicable modifiers).

Default values are **renderer-owned and platform-appropriate**; the tables below
name the tokens and their *meaning*, never concrete values. The renderer MUST
resolve tokens by name and MAY map them onto native semantic resources (e.g. the
platform's system text color for `color.text.primary`).

### Colors — Tier 1

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `color.primary` | Primary brand / accent fill |
| `color.secondary` | Secondary brand / accent fill |
| `color.background` | Document / canvas background |
| `color.surface` | Raised surface (cards, panels, popovers) |
| `color.text.primary` | Primary text color |
| `color.text.secondary` | Secondary / muted text color |
| `color.text.onPrimary` | Text placed on a `color.primary` fill |
| `color.border` | Default border / outline color |
| `color.accent` | Accent for controls (focus, selection, toggle fill) |

Tier 2: `color.separator` (hairline dividers), and status colors
`color.success`, `color.warning`, `color.danger`, `color.info`.

### Typography — Tier 1 core

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `font.body.size` | Body text size |
| `font.body.weight` | Body text weight (100–900) |
| `font.body.family` | Body font family (STRING) |

Tier 2: `font.body.lineHeight`, `font.caption.size`,
`font.heading.1.size`–`font.heading.6.size` (with matching `.weight`/`.family`
paths), `font.mono.family`.

The **predefined typographies** (`TEXT_STYLE`: `LargeTitle`…`Caption2`,
spec/MODIFIERS.md §2) are the semantic counterparts of these token paths: the
renderer owns their concrete size/weight (a baked per-renderer HIG scale). An
application that wants full control can instead bind text to a `TEXT_STYLE` of
its own via the `font.<style>.*` token paths above, or set an explicit
`FONT_SIZE`/`FONT_WEIGHT`/`FONT_FAMILY` override on top.

### Spacing — Tier 1

Spacing is a **generative family** (Tailwind-v4 style): one base unit
multiplied by an arbitrary number.

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `space.base` | The spacing **unit** (F32) — override this to change the whole density |
| `space.<N>` | `space.base` × N, where N is any positive decimal (`space.1`, `space.2`, `space.0.5`, `space.3.75`) — **computed** by the resolver |

Rules:

1. The `space.<N>` family is **generative**, not independently valued: the
   renderer resolves `space.base` and multiplies by the numeric leaf. Individual
   members MUST NOT be overridden via `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` — override `space.base`
   to control the whole scale.
2. The color-scheme layer and parent fallback apply to `space.base`, never to an
   individual `space.<N>` member (`dark.space.2` is not a token; the dark layer
   is `dark.space.base`).
3. A spacing/padding property MAY carry a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference to any
   `space.<N>` path — e.g. a DSL expresses `.padding(space.2)` or `Space(2)`.
   Literal F32 spacing values remain valid and unthemed.

Tier 2: `size.control.xs` / `sm` / `md` / `lg` — standard control heights.

### Radius (roundings) — Tier 1

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `radius.xs` / `radius.sm` / `radius.md` / `radius.lg` / `radius.xl` | Corner radius scale (F32) |
| `radius.full` | Fully round (pill/circle) — renderer resolves to its "infinite" value |

### Borders — Tier 1 core

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `border.width.thin` | Default hairline/border width |

Tier 2: `border.width.thick`.

### Elevation — Tier 2

Shadows are composite; each component is its own token:

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `elevation.low.color` / `radius` / `x` / `y` / `blur` | Low elevation shadow |
| `elevation.high.color` / `radius` / `x` / `y` / `blur` | High elevation shadow |

### Opacity — Tier 2

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `opacity.disabled` | The renderer MAY apply this to disabled controls. The disabled **state** itself is the `ENABLED` property; its visual handling (including this opacity) remains renderer-owned. |

### Shared control core — Tier 1

Tokens every control-style component (buttons, inputs, switches, sliders, …)
shares. Renderers MUST resolve these; an individual token a renderer cannot
apply is ignored.

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `control.background` | Control resting background |
| `control.foreground` | Control content (label/icon) color |
| `control.border` | Control border color |
| `control.border.width` | Control border width |
| `control.radius` | Control corner radius |
| `control.padding.horizontal` / `control.padding.vertical` | Control inner padding |
| `control.height` | Control height (F32) |
| `control.font.size` / `control.font.weight` | Control text |
| `control.accent` | Control accent (fill, selection, focus) |

### Per-component tokens

Small sets; only where a component's semantics genuinely differ from
`control.*`. All Tier 1 unless noted.

**Buttons** (Tier 1): `button.background`, `button.foreground`, `button.border`,
`button.radius`, `button.padding`, `button.height`, `button.font.size`,
`button.font.weight`, `button.accent`.

**Text fields / editors** (Tier 1): `input.background`, `input.foreground`,
`input.placeholder`, `input.border`, `input.radius`, `input.font.size`.

**Toggle / switch** (Tier 1): `toggle.accent`, `toggle.track.off`,
`toggle.track.on`, `toggle.thumb`.

**Slider** (Tier 1): `slider.accent`, `slider.track`, `slider.thumb`.

**Progress / gauge** (Tier 1): `progress.track`, `progress.fill`,
`gauge.track`, `gauge.fill`.

**Stepper** (Tier 2): `stepper.accent`, `stepper.background`, `stepper.border`,
`stepper.radius`.

**Picker** (Tier 2): `picker.accent`, `picker.background`, `picker.border`,
`picker.radius`.

**Menu** (Tier 2): `menu.background`, `menu.foreground`, `menu.border`,
`menu.radius`.

**Label** (Tier 2): `label.foreground`, `label.font.size`.

---

## Color Schemes (Light / Dark)

Base token paths define the **light** design. A `dark.`-prefixed path defines
the **dark** design for the same token.

The renderer derives the **effective color scheme** from its platform's native
light/dark signal — it is **never** carried by the protocol.

### Rules

1. **Base = light.** `color.primary` is the light value; `dark.color.primary`
   is the dark value.
2. A renderer MUST provide **both** light and dark defaults for every Tier 1
   token (platform-appropriate). Dark mode therefore works even when the
   application only overrides base tokens.
3. The application rolls a full theme by overriding base values and — where the
   dark look must differ — `dark.*` values.
4. The renderer MUST **re-resolve** every token-referencing property when the
   effective scheme changes, and MAY animate the transition.
5. The `dark.` prefix is the first scheme prefix; the namespace is open so
   custom schemes could follow. Only `light` (base) and `dark` are
   standardized.

---

## Resolution

```
FUNCTION resolveToken(tokenPath, scheme):
    # Walk most-specific → least-specific, applying the dark layer first.
    layers = []
    if scheme == dark:
        layers += [dark.path, dark.parent(path), …dark.root]   # dark.* layer
    layers += [path, parent(path), …root]                       # base layer

    for candidate in layers:
        if appOverrides.has(candidate):
            return appOverrides[candidate]
    for candidate in layers:
        if rendererDefaults.has(candidate):
            return rendererDefaults[candidate]
    return fallbackValue(path)
```

Example — `color.primary` with the **dark** scheme active and only
`dark.color.primary` overridden:

1. `dark.color.primary` — app override → **used**.
2. (Unreached) `color.primary` app override, `dark.color.primary` renderer
   default, etc.

With the **light** scheme active:

1. `color.primary` — app override, else renderer default, else parent/fallback.
   The `dark.*` layer is skipped entirely.

### Generative token families

A **generative family** is a token rule rather than an independent value. Today
the `space` family is generative: `space.<N>` resolves by resolving `space.base`
(the scheme layer and parent fallback apply there) and multiplying by the
numeric leaf parsed from the path. This lets one override (`space.base`) drive
an arbitrarily fine spacing scale without per-step tokens. Only the `space`
family is generative today; other families could follow.

---

## References in properties

Any property whose value type is `COLOR` / `F32` / `STRING` / `ENUM` MAY instead
carry the **`DESIGN_TOKEN`** value type (`0x08`), with `C` = arenaRef to the
token path. The renderer resolves the reference against the token tables and the
current scheme, and re-resolves when the scheme changes.

- This is how a DSL expresses *semantic intent*: `.foregroundStyle(.primary)`
  or `Color.token("color.primary")` emits a token reference, not a packed color.
- A literal value and a token reference are mutually exclusive on a property.
- Because overrides and the scheme are renderer state, a token-typed property
  requires **no re-emission** when a token changes — the renderer re-resolves.

---

## Renderer Responsibilities

A renderer MUST:

1. Provide platform-appropriate **light and dark defaults** for all Tier 1
   tokens.
2. Accept `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` commands and store overrides.
3. Derive the effective color scheme from the platform and re-resolve on change.
4. Resolve token references (`DESIGN_TOKEN` value type) in properties.
5. Fall back to defaults when no override exists.
6. Never transmit visual styling rules in the protocol.

A renderer MAY:

- Map tokens onto native semantic resources (system colors, platform
  typography) for its defaults.
- **Ignore** individual tokens it cannot apply (Tier 2, or Tier 1 tokens
  without a native equivalent) — the "allowed and ignored" rule modifiers use.
- Quantize / approximate token values to platform capabilities (e.g. RGB565
  color depth on embedded displays, limited font sets).

An application MAY override any token via `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` (base and `dark.*`)
and reference any token in a property; it MUST NOT assume specific default
values.

---

## Renderer Integration Contract

A future native renderer adopts the token system by implementing five pieces:

1. **Default token table** — Tier 1 light + dark defaults from native resources.
2. **Scheme detection** — the platform's native light/dark signal.
3. **Resolution** — the override → default → parent → fallback algorithm, with
   the `dark.*` layer keyed on the effective scheme.
4. **Property resolution** — any property carrying a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference
   resolves to the concrete native value (e.g. a dynamic system color / theme
   resource / style value).
5. **Re-resolution** — on scheme change, re-resolve and update the rendered
   output; animate if native.

The same contract powers the reference renderers (`pathland-render-html`,
`pathland-render-gtk`, the JS DOM renderer) and is checked in their `status.md`
files.

99: /// The host's native-element description of a rendered tree.
100: #[derive(Debug)]
101: pub struct RenderTree {
102:     /// nodeId -> node.
103:     pub nodes: HashMap<u32, HostNode>,
104:     /// Design-token overrides (`PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`), base (light) values
105:     /// keyed by full path.
106:     overrides: BTreeMap<String, TokenValue>,
107:     /// `dark.*` overrides keyed by the bare path (the prefix stripped).
108:     dark_overrides: BTreeMap<String, TokenValue>,
109:     /// Renderer default token values (Tier 1 light + dark, spec/TOKENS.md) —
110:     /// concrete platform-appropriate fallbacks. A renderer may enrich these
111:     /// with native theme colors (e.g. GTK `@theme_*` named colors) via
112:     /// [`RenderTree::set_defaults`].
113:     defaults: BTreeMap<String, TokenValue>,
114:     dark_defaults: BTreeMap<String, TokenValue>,
115:     /// The effective color scheme (renderer-derived, never carried by the
116:     /// protocol).
117:     scheme: Scheme,
118: }
119: 
120: impl Default for RenderTree {
121:     fn default() -> Self {
122:         let (defaults, dark_defaults) = concrete_default_tables();
123:         Self {
124:             nodes: HashMap::new(),
125:             overrides: BTreeMap::new(),
126:             dark_overrides: BTreeMap::new(),
127:             defaults,
128:             dark_defaults,
129:             scheme: Scheme::Light,
130:         }
131:     }
132: }

134: impl RenderTree {
135:     /// Install renderer default token tables (see [`RenderTree::defaults`]).
136:     pub fn set_defaults(
137:         &mut self,
138:         defaults: BTreeMap<String, TokenValue>,
139:         dark_defaults: BTreeMap<String, TokenValue>,
140:     ) {
141:         self.defaults = defaults;
142:         self.dark_defaults = dark_defaults;
143:         self.resolve_tokens();
144:     }
145: 
146:     /// The effective color scheme.
147:     pub fn scheme(&self) -> Scheme {
148:         self.scheme
149:     }
150: 
151:     /// Set the effective color scheme and re-resolve every token-referencing
152:     /// property (spec/TOKENS.md resolution contract).
153:     pub fn set_scheme(&mut self, scheme: Scheme) {
154:         self.scheme = scheme;
155:         self.resolve_tokens();
156:     }
157: 
158:     /// Re-resolve every `DESIGN_TOKEN`-typed property against the theme, the
159:     /// active scheme, and the parent-fallback chain, materializing concrete
160:     /// values into [`HostNode::properties`] (numeric) or [`HostNode::strings`]
161:     /// (STRING tokens). The paths are kept in [`HostNode::token_refs`] for
162:     /// re-resolution on scheme change.
163:     pub fn resolve_tokens(&mut self) {
164:         let tables = TokenTables {
165:             overrides: &self.overrides,
166:             dark_overrides: &self.dark_overrides,
167:             defaults: &self.defaults,
168:             dark_defaults: &self.dark_defaults,
169:         };
170:         for node in self.nodes.values_mut() {
171:             let refs: Vec<(u16, String)> = node.token_refs.iter().map(|(k, v)| (*k, v.clone())).collect();
172:             for (prop, path) in refs {
173:                 if let Some(value) = resolve_token(&path, self.scheme, &tables) {
174:                     match value {
175:                         TokenValue::Str(s) => {
176:                             node.strings.insert(prop, s);
177:                         }
178:                         _ => {
179:                             if let Some(bits) = value.to_bits() {
180:                                 node.properties.insert(prop, bits);
181:                             }
182:                         }
183:                     }
184:                 }
185:             }
186:         }
187:     }
188: 
189:     /// Apply a frame's opcodes to this tree (a delta).
190:     pub fn apply_frame(&mut self, frame: &Frame<'_>) {
191:         for op in frame.opcodes() {
192:             match (op.category(), op.command()) {
193:                 (category::TREE, tree::CREATE_NODE) => {
194:                     let id = op.a();
195:                     let ty = op.b() as u16;
196:                     let entry = self.nodes.entry(id).or_default();
197:                     entry.id = id;
198:                     entry.component_type = ty;
199:                 }
200:                 (category::TREE, tree::DELETE_NODE) => {
201:                     self.nodes.remove(&op.a());
202:                 }
203:                 (category::TREE, tree::INSERT_CHILD) => {
204:                     let (parent, child) = (op.a(), op.b());
205:                     if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
206:                         if !p.children.contains(&child) {
207:                             p.children.push(child);
208:                         }
209:                     }
210:                     if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
211:                         c.parent = Some(parent);
212:                     }
213:                 }
214:                 (category::TREE, tree::REMOVE_CHILD) => {
215:                     let (parent, child) = (op.a(), op.b());
216:                     if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
217:                         p.children.retain(|c| *c != child);
218:                     }
219:                     if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
220:                         c.parent = None;
221:                     }
222:                 }
223:                 (category::TREE, tree::MOVE_CHILD) => {
224:                     let (parent, child, new_index) = (op.a(), op.b(), op.c() as usize);
225:                     if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
226:                         if let Some(pos) = p.children.iter().position(|c| *c == child) {
227:                             p.children.remove(pos);
228:                         }
229:                         let idx = if new_index == usize::MAX {
230:                             p.children.len()
231:                         } else {
232:                             new_index.min(p.children.len())
233:                         };
234:                         p.children.insert(idx, child);
235:                     }
236:                 }
237:                 (category::PARAMETER, parameter::SET_PROPERTY) => {
238:                     let prop_id = op.b() as u16;
239:                     let vt = (op.b() >> 16) as u8;
240:                     if let Some(n) = self.nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
241:                         if vt == value_type::STRING {
242:                             // Resolve the arena offset into the actual text.
243:                             if let Ok(text) = frame.arena_str(op.c()) {
244:                                 n.strings.insert(prop_id, text.to_string());
245:                             }
246:                         } else if vt == value_type::DESIGN_TOKEN {
247:                             // A token reference: keep the path for resolution
248:                             // against the theme (spec/TOKENS.md). C is the arena
249:                             // offset of the token path.
250:                             if let Ok(path) = frame.arena_str(op.c()) {
251:                                 n.token_refs.insert(prop_id, path.to_string());
252:                             }
253:                         } else if vt == value_type::LIST {
254:                             // An arena-backed `[u32 count][f32 × count]` array —
255:                             // today a SIZE_THAT_FITS `FIT_QUERY` table.
256:                             if let Ok(bytes) = frame.arena_get(op.c()) {
257:                                 if let Some(values) = list_f32(bytes) {
258:                                     n.lists.insert(prop_id, values);
259:                                 }
260:                             }
261:                         } else {
262:                             n.properties.insert(prop_id, op.c());
263:                         }
264:                     }
265:                 }
266:                 (category::PARAMETER, parameter::SET_TEXT) => {
267:                     if let Some(n) = self.nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
268:                         n.text = frame.arena_str(op.b()).ok().map(|s| s.to_string());
269:                     }
270:                 }
271:                 (category::PARAMETER, parameter::SET_DATE) => {
272:                     // A = node, B = days since epoch (I32), C = millis of day.
273:                     if let Some(n) = self.nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
274:                         n.date = Some((op.b() as i32, op.c()));
275:                     }
276:                 }
277:                 (category::PARAMETER, parameter::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN) => {
278:                     // Global override: A = arenaRef (token path), B = valueType,
279:                     // C = value (for STRING, an arenaRef to the value string).
280:                     if let Ok(path) = frame.arena_str(op.a()) {
281:                         let vt = (op.b() & 0xFF) as u8;
282:                         let value = if vt == value_type::STRING {
283:                             frame
284:                                 .arena_str(op.c())
285:                                 .map(|s| TokenValue::Str(s.to_string()))
286:                                 .unwrap_or(TokenValue::U32(0))
287:                         } else {
288:                             TokenValue::from_wire(vt, op.c()).unwrap_or(TokenValue::U32(op.c()))
289:                         };
290:                         if let Some(bare) = path.strip_prefix("dark.") {
291:                             self.dark_overrides.insert(bare.to_string(), value);
292:                         } else {
293:                             self.overrides.insert(path.to_string(), value);
294:                         }
295:                     }
296:                 }
297:                 _ => {}
298:             }
299:         }
300:         self.resolve_tokens();
301:     }

314: /// Read a length-prefixed f32 array (`[u32 count][f32 × count]`) from an arena
315: /// entry — the numeric form of a `LIST`-typed value (spec/OPCODE.md).
316: fn list_f32(entry: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<f32>> {
317:     if entry.len() < 4 {
318:         return None;
319:     }
320:     let count = u32::from_le_bytes(entry[..4].try_into().ok()?) as usize;
321:     let start = 4;
322:     if start + count * 4 > entry.len() {
323:         return None;
324:     }
325:     let mut values = Vec::with_capacity(count);
326:     for i in 0..count {
327:         let bits = u32::from_le_bytes(entry[start + i * 4..start + i * 4 + 4].try_into().ok()?);
328:         values.push(f32::from_bits(bits));
329:     }
330:     Some(values)
331: }

448: /// Convert a single opcode into a human-readable line (debugging aid).
449: pub fn describe(op: &Opcode) -> String {
450:     match (op.category(), op.command()) {
451:         (category::TREE, tree::CREATE_NODE) => {
452:             format!("TREE:CREATE_NODE id={} type=0x{:04x}", op.a(), op.b() as u16)
453:         }
454:         (category::TREE, tree::DELETE_NODE) => format!("TREE:DELETE_NODE id={}", op.a()),
455:         (category::TREE, tree::INSERT_CHILD) => format!(
456:             "TREE:INSERT_CHILD parent={} child={} index={}",
457:             op.a(),
458:             op.b(),
459:             op.c()
460:         ),
461:         (category::TREE, tree::REMOVE_CHILD) => {
462:             format!("TREE:REMOVE_CHILD parent={} child={}", op.a(), op.b())
463:         }
464:         (category::TREE, tree::MOVE_CHILD) => format!(
465:             "TREE:MOVE_CHILD parent={} child={} index={}",
466:             op.a(),
467:             op.b(),
468:             op.c()
469:         ),
470:         (category::PARAMETER, parameter::SET_PROPERTY) => format!(
471:             "PARAMETER:SET_PROPERTY id={} prop=0x{:04x} value=0x{:08x}",
472:             op.a(),
473:             op.b() as u16,
474:             op.c()
475:         ),
476:         (category::PARAMETER, parameter::SET_TEXT) => {
477:             format!("PARAMETER:SET_TEXT id={} arenaRef={}", op.a(), op.b())
478:         }
479:         (category::PARAMETER, parameter::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN) => format!(
480:             "PARAMETER:SET_DESIGN_TOKEN pathArenaRef={} valueType=0x{:02x} value=0x{:08x}",
481:             op.a(),
482:             op.b() & 0xFF,
483:             op.c()
484:         ),
485:         _ => format!("{:?}", op),
486:     }
487: }

583:             "playing was set before the emit"
584:         );
585: 
586:         let surface = tree
587:             .nodes
588:             .values()
589:             .find(|n| n.component_type == component_type::VIDEO)
590:             .expect("the video surface");
591:         assert_eq!(
592:             surface.u32_property(pathland_core::property_id::MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID, 0),
593:             controller.id,
594:             "the surface points at the controller's node"
595:         );
596:     }
597: 
598:     /// `LIST` (`FIT_QUERY`) and `SET_DATE` decode into the shared tree, so the
599:     /// Qt renderer can measure a fit slot and format a date (spec/PRIMITIVES.md).
600:     #[test]
601:     fn decodes_list_and_date_values() {
602:         // The ring arena entry is `[u32 byteLen][payload]` (Guest::alloc); a
603:         // LIST payload is `[u32 count][f32 × count]` (spec/OPCODE.md).
604:         let mut payload = Vec::new();
605:         payload.extend_from_slice(&2u32.to_le_bytes());
606:         payload.extend_from_slice(&320.0f32.to_bits().to_le_bytes());
607:         payload.extend_from_slice(&640.0f32.to_bits().to_le_bytes());
608:         let mut arena = Vec::new();
609:         arena.extend_from_slice(&(payload.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
610:         arena.extend_from_slice(&payload);
611: 
612:         let ops = [
613:             Opcode::new(
614:                 category::TREE,
615:                 tree::CREATE_NODE,
616:                 0,
617:                 1,
618:                 component_type::SIZE_THAT_FITS as u32,
619:                 0,
620:             ),
621:             Opcode::new(
622:                 category::PARAMETER,
623:                 parameter::SET_PROPERTY,
624:                 0,
625:                 1,
626:                 ((value_type::LIST as u32) << 16)
627:                     | pathland_core::property_id::FIT_QUERY as u32,
628:                 0,
629:             ),
630:             Opcode::new(category::PARAMETER, parameter::SET_DATE, 0, 1, 19_723, 3_600_000),
631:         ];
632:         let slots: Vec<u8> = ops.iter().flat_map(|o| o.to_bytes()).collect();
633:         let frame = Frame::from_parts(&slots, &arena, 0, slots.len());
634:         let tree = render_tree_from_frame(&frame);
635: 
636:         let node = tree.node(1).unwrap();
637:         assert_eq!(
638:             node.list_property(pathland_core::property_id::FIT_QUERY),
639:             Some([320.0f32, 640.0].as_slice())
640:         );
641:         assert_eq!(node.date, Some((19_723, 3_600_000)));
642:     }
643: 
644:     #[test]
645:     fn applies_a_delta_frame() {
646:         let layout = MemoryLayout::default();
647:         let mut mem = vec![0u8; layout.total_bytes()];
648:         init_memory(&mut mem, &layout);
649: 
650:         let mut engine = Engine::new();
651:         let mut tree = RenderTree::default();
652: 
653:         let mut a = vstack![text("ab")]
654:             .with(|v| {
655:                 v.spacing(4.0);
656:             })
657:             .modifiers(Padding(8.0))
658:             .build();
659:         assign_ids(&mut a, &mut 1);
660:         {
661:             let mut guest = Guest::new(&mut mem, &layout);
662:             guest.begin_frame();
663:             engine.emit(&a, &mut guest).unwrap();
664:             guest.end_frame();
665:         }
666:         {
667:             let mut host = pathland_core::Host::new(&mut mem, &layout);
668:             tree.apply_frame(&host.frames()[0]);
669:         }
670: 
671:         // Delta: spacing 4 -> 12.
672:         let mut b = vstack![text("ab")]
673:             .with(|v| {
674:                 v.spacing(12.0);
675:             })
676:             .modifiers(Padding(8.0))
677:             .build();
678:         assign_ids(&mut b, &mut 1);
679:         {
680:             let mut guest = Guest::new(&mut mem, &layout);
681:             guest.begin_frame();
682:             engine.emit(&b, &mut guest).unwrap();
683:             guest.end_frame();
684:         }
685:         {
686:             let mut host = pathland_core::Host::new(&mut mem, &layout);
687:             tree.apply_frame(&host.frames()[0]);
688:         }
689: 
690:         assert_eq!(tree.nodes.len(), 2);
691:         let root = tree.node(1).unwrap();
692:         assert_eq!(
693:             root.properties.get(&pathland_core::property_id::SPACING),
694:             Some(&12.0f32.to_bits())
695:         );
696:     }
697: 
698:     #[test]
699:     fn string_properties_resolve_from_frame() {
700:         use pathland_core::{Guest, Host, MemoryLayout, init_memory, property_id, value_type};
701: 
702:         let layout = MemoryLayout::default();
703:         let mut mem = vec![0u8; layout.total_bytes()];
704:         init_memory(&mut mem, &layout);
705: 
706:         {
707:             let mut guest = Guest::new(&mut mem, &layout);
708:             guest.begin_frame();
709:             guest.create_node(1, component_type::IMAGE).unwrap();
710:             let ref_src = guest.alloc_str("assets/logo.png").unwrap();
711:             guest
712:                 .set_property(1, property_id::IMAGE_SOURCE, value_type::STRING, ref_src)
713:                 .unwrap();
714:             guest.end_frame();
715:         }
716:         {
717:             let mut host = Host::new(&mut mem, &layout);
718:             let mut tree = RenderTree::default();
719:             tree.apply_frame(&host.frames()[0]);
720: 
721:             let n = tree.node(1).unwrap();
722:             assert_eq!(n.component_type, component_type::IMAGE);
723:             // The STRING property is resolved to its text...
724:             assert_eq!(
725:                 n.string_property(property_id::IMAGE_SOURCE),
726:                 Some("assets/logo.png")
727:             );
728:             // ...and is NOT stored as a raw arena offset in `properties`.
729:             assert!(!n.properties.contains_key(&property_id::IMAGE_SOURCE));
730:         }
731:     }
732: }

display.text:
# pathland-render-core — implementation status

**Last updated:** September 23, 2026

The **toolkit-free renderer core shared by every Pathland renderer** (GTK4, Qt,
…): opcode-frame decode into a retained native-element description
(`RenderTree` / `HostNode`) plus the design-token resolution contract
(spec/TOKENS.md). Protocol contract: `spec/`. This crate touches **no toolkit**
(no GTK, no Qt) — it is pure protocol + tokens.

## Implemented

- **`RenderTree` / `HostNode`** (extracted from `pathland-render-gtk`'s
  `host.rs`, which was already GTK-free):
  - `TREE` ops → node tree: `CREATE_NODE`, `DELETE_NODE`, `INSERT_CHILD`,
    `REMOVE_CHILD`, `MOVE_CHILD` (append/insert at `u32::MAX`), parent/child
    bookkeeping.
  - `STYLE` ops → node properties: `SET_PROPERTY` (numeric `properties`,
    `STRING` resolved from the arena into `strings`, `DESIGN_TOKEN` refs kept
    in `token_refs`), `SET_TEXT`, `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` (global overrides, base +
    `dark.` split).
  - Node accessors: `node(id)`, `root()`, string/f32/u32 property helpers,
    `checked()`.
- **Design tokens (spec/TOKENS.md renderer contract)**:
  - `STYLE::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides stored (base + `dark.*` by path
    prefix; STRING-valued overrides resolved from the arena).
  - `DESIGN_TOKEN`-typed `SET_PROPERTY` values record the token path and
    **resolve at apply time** against the theme, the active scheme, and the
    parent-fallback chain into concrete `properties`/`strings`
    (`resolve_tokens`, reusing `pathland_core::tokens`); paths are kept for
    re-resolution on scheme change.
  - **Tier-1 default tables** (light + dark) via `concrete_default_tables` —
    concrete platform-appropriate fallbacks; a renderer may enrich with native
    theme colors via `RenderTree::set_defaults`.
  - `set_scheme` re-resolves every token-referencing property. Scheme is never
    carried by the protocol.
- **`render_tree_from_frame`** — decode a fresh tree from one frame.
- **`describe`** — one-opcode human-readable line (debugging aid).

## Consumed by

- `pathland-render-gtk` (decode + token resolution; the GTK-specific
  `tokens.rs` GTK theme-color enrichment stays in that crate).
- `pathland-render-qt` (planned).
- `pathland-view-native` and `pathland-core-transport` dev-tests (decode a
  frame into a `RenderTree` without pulling in a toolkit).

## Not implemented / gaps

- No layout computation (by design — the protocol never emits rects).
- No META handling (`RESET`/`ENVIRONMENT`/`RESYNC`) — renderer-owned concern.

## Verified by

`cargo test -p pathland-render-core` — decode of a declarative frame (no
layout/rect data present), delta-frame application (unchanged nodes preserved),
and STRING property resolution from the arena. Full decode/token coverage also
runs through `pathland-render-gtk`'s tests (`cargo test`).

1: # pathland-render-gtk — implementation status
2: 
3: **Last updated:** October 15, 2026
4: 
5: The **GTK4 renderer**: maps opcode frames incrementally onto native GTK widgets
6: (shared-memory desktop path). Protocol contract: `spec/`. Design-token contract:
7: `spec/TOKENS.md`.
8: 
9: **Note (2026-09-23):** the toolkit-free decode core (`RenderTree`/`HostNode`,
10: `apply_frame`, token tables + resolution, `concrete_default_tables`,
11: `render_tree_from_frame`, `describe`) moved to the shared
12: `pathland-render-core` crate; this crate now consumes it and keeps the
13: GTK-specific layers (`tokens.rs` native-theme enrichment, `layout.rs`,
14: `capi.rs`). `pathland_gtk::RenderTree` etc. remain re-exported for
15: compatibility.
16: 
17: ## Implemented
18: 
19: - **Components → widgets** (`widget_kind`/`build_widget`):
20:   - `VSTACK`/`HSTACK`/`LAZY_VSTACK`/`LAZY_HSTACK` → `GtkBox` (spacing/alignment/
21:     padding/content-margins),
22:   - `PROXY_VIEW` (spec/PROXY.md) → `GtkBox` (a transparent container): the spliced
23:     (id-remapped) origin subtree lays out in place,
24:   - `TEXT` → `GtkLabel` (text; `TEXT_STYLE`/`FONT_SIZE`/`FONT_WEIGHT`/
25:     `FONT_FAMILY`/`FONT_DESIGN`/`COLOR` via a Pango `FontDescription`/
26:     attributes),
27:   - `BUTTON` → `GtkButton` (label; composite body when it has children),
28:   - `ICON` → `GtkImage` (the canonical `ICON_NAME` maps through this renderer's
29:     own `gtk_icon_name` map to an Adwaita symbolic icon name; `FONT_SIZE` → pixel size,
30:     `COLOR` → CSS tint; unmapped names fall back to `image-missing`),
31:   - `GRID`/`LAZY_VGRID`/`LAZY_HGRID` → `GtkGrid` (row-major cells from child
32:     index + `WIDTH` column count),
33:   - `SCROLLVIEW` → `GtkScrolledWindow` (single child),
34:   - `ZSTACK` → `GtkOverlay`,
35:   - `SPACER` → expanding box, `IMAGE` → `GtkPicture` (`IMAGE_SOURCE`),
36:   - `TOGGLE` → `GtkSwitch`/`GtkCheckButton`/`GtkToggleButton` by `TOGGLE_STYLE`
37:     (`SELECTED` ↔ active),
38:   - `SLIDER` → `GtkScale` (`VALUE`/`MIN`/`MAX`/`STEP`),
39:   - `TEXT_FIELD` → `GtkEntry` (`LABEL`/`PROMPT`/`IS_SECURE`),
40:   - `TEXT_EDITOR` → `GtkTextView` (multi-line),
41:   - `COLOR` → `GtkDrawingArea` (solid fill), `SHAPE` → `GtkDrawingArea`
42:     (`SHAPE_KIND`), `DIVIDER` → `GtkSeparator`,
43:   - `PROGRESS_VIEW` → `GtkProgressBar`/`GtkSpinner`,
44:   - `GAUGE` → `GtkLevelBar`, `STEPPER` → `GtkSpinButton`,
45:   - `DATE_PICKER` → `GtkCalendar`, `PICKER` → `GtkDropDown` (option children +
46:     `SELECTION`), `MENU` → `GtkMenuButton`, `COLOR_PICKER` → `GtkColorButton`.
47:   Unknown components → blank `GtkLabel`.
48: - **Container + composite reconciliation** (diff-guarded): stacks/grid/scroll/
49:   overlay children, and **Composite Override Mode** for `BUTTON`/`TOGGLE`/`MENU`
50:   with children (custom body wrapped in the native button shell). A `BUTTON`
51:   composite body is a **horizontal row** with centered children (matching the
52:   HTML renderer's `.pathland-button` `inline-flex`); `TOGGLE`/`MENU` bodies stay
53:   vertical (HTML wraps those as block/inline-block). A composite control **sizes
54:   to its content on the main axis** (the button's main-axis `valign`/`halign` is
55:   `Center`, mirroring HTML's `inline-flex`) unless the node is explicitly
56:   `FILL`-sized — otherwise the enclosing box's default `Fill` alignment stretches
57:   it (e.g. a library row button absorbs the viewport height, inflating
58:   fixed-size images). A **`VIDEO` surface** with children (a custom
59:   `VideoStyle` body, spec DSL.md §5.7) is a container too: its
60:   control children reconcile into the media container box. Control-level
61:   `COLOR`/`FONT_SIZE`/`TEXT_STYLE` are
62:   emitted as CSS (`color`, `font-size`, `font-weight`, `font-family`) so they
63:   **cascade** to the content's child labels (e.g. `.foregroundStyle`/`.fontSize`
64:   on a composite Button).
65: - **Style properties**: `VISIBLE`, `OPACITY`, `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`,
66:   `CONTENT_MARGINS`, `PADDING` + per-edge, `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, `BORDER_WIDTH`/
67:   `COLOR`/`RADIUS`, `FONT_FAMILY`/`FONT_WEIGHT`/`FONT_DESIGN` (CSS provider),
68:   `COLOR`, `FONT_SIZE`, `TEXT_STYLE` (renderer-owned default size/weight; an
69:   explicit `FONT_SIZE`/`FONT_WEIGHT` overrides the corresponding axis).
70: - **Fixed-size images scale to the points box**: a `WIDTH`×`HEIGHT` on an
71:   `IMAGE` is a **logical-points box** (spec/OPCODE.md §units), and `GtkPicture`'s
72:   natural size is its content's intrinsic pixels — so a finite box was only a
73:   *minimum* request and the cover rendered at its intrinsic size. A fixed-size
74:   image now decodes and scales the content into the box (via gdk-pixbuf), making
75:   the picture's natural size equal the requested points (the bar cover renders
76:   36pt, the sidebar 220pt, the bar stays 76pt tall). `CONTENT_MODE` is honored:
77:   `Fit` → scale-to-fit + centered on a transparent canvas (letterbox, like
78:   `object-fit:contain`), `Fill` → scale-to-cover + center-crop (like
79:   `object-fit:cover`); absent → Fit. The scaled box is cached per node (steady
80:   state doesn't re-decode). A non-fixed (`FILL`/single-axis) image keeps the
81:   native `set_filename` loader. Retina *crispness* (decoding at the display
82:   scale factor) is a documented follow-up — layout is points-correct on every
83:   display.
84: - **`FILL` expansion**: a `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` of `FILL` (-1.0, SwiftUI
85:   `maxWidth/maxHeight: .infinity`) now sets `hexpand`/`vexpand` + `Fill` axis
86:   alignment so arbitrary elements truly expand to the available space; a finite
87:   value is a size request and `HUG_CONTENT` leaves the natural size.
88: - **Events**: pointer `POINTER_DOWN`/`MOVE`/`UP` via `GestureClick`/
89:   `EventControllerMotion` (`EVENT_LISTENERS`-driven), plus **value/text events**
90:   (`VALUE_CHANGED` from toggle/slider/picker, `TEXT_CHANGED` from text field)
91:   **gated by `BINDING_ID`** (transport-aware event guards), sent through the
92:   two-way event arena.
93: - **In-flight interaction (spec EVENTS.md)**: a capture-phase `GestureClick`
94:   on a `SLIDER` marks the drag session (`drag_state`); while a slider is being
95:   dragged, inbound `VALUE` writes are **suppressed** (the drag position is
96:   user-authoritative, so a server echo can't flicker the thumb), and the
97:   session boundaries are reported as **`EDITING_CHANGED`** (press/release) and
98:   **`FOCUS_CHANGED`** (`EventControllerFocus` enter/leave) when the node
99:   declares the `LISTEN_EDITING`/`LISTEN_FOCUS` bits — the app-side escape
100:   hatch to suppress echoes of any derived state during a session. Because a
101:   `GtkScale`'s own drag gesture can consume the button release, sliders also
102:   end the session via a **settle fallback**: each user `value-changed` during
103:   a drag re-arms a ~150 ms timer that, when the drag settles, clears the
104:   session and reports `EDITING_CHANGED(false)` — so an app's seek-on-release
105:   commits even when `GestureClick::released` never fires.
106: - **Platform back / `NAVIGATE`**: a window-level `EventControllerKey`
107:   (capture phase, attached once in `run_with_pump`) maps Escape — and
108:   BackSpace when no text entry has focus — to `Event::Navigate { url: None }`
109:   through the shared event sink. `NAVIGATE` is global (never node-keyed),
110:   matching spec/EVENTS.md.
111: - **Native navigation slot (`AdwNavigationView`)**: a stack node carrying the
112:   `ROUTE` property (a `NavigationContainer`, spec/DSL.md §4.5) renders as an
113:   `AdwNavigationView` instead of a `GtkBox`. The adapter reconciles its page
114:   stack **by depth** (`NAV_DEPTH` 0x201A, U32): it pops pages down to the
115:   app's depth, then **pushes** when the route is deeper (normal push / deep
116:   link), **replaces the top page** when the depth is unchanged and the route
117:   differs (a guard redirect / `replace()`), and **refreshes in place** when the
118:   visible page already shows the route (a signal update, or a re-emit after a
119:   user-initiated back). In the default chrome mode (`NAV_CHROME` 0x201B
120:   `PlatformDefault`, or missing) each page wraps the destination in a
121:   `ToolbarView` + `HeaderBar` (`show-back-button`) — the native top bar and
122:   back button; in `Custom` chrome mode (`Chrome.CUSTOM` → `NAV_CHROME=1`) the
123:   page child is the bare destination (the developer owns all nav UI). The
124:   header-bar back button's `popped` signal drops the
125:   page from the adapter's mirror and emits `Event::Navigate { url: None }`
126:   (suppressed during renderer-driven pops), so native back and Escape both flow
127:   into the app's `router.pop()`. The back-stack stays app-owned; the
128:   `AdwNavigationView` is only the renderer's rendered-output cache.
129:   `libadwaita` (0.7, `v1_4` feature) is a new native dependency.
130: - **Design tokens / theming (spec/TOKENS.md renderer contract)**:
131:   - `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides are stored (`host.rs`), base + `dark.*`
132:     split by path prefix; STRING-valued overrides resolve the value string from
133:     the arena.
134:   - `DESIGN_TOKEN`-typed `SET_PROPERTY` values record the token path
135:     (`HostNode::token_refs`) and **resolve at apply time** against the theme,
136:     the active scheme, and the parent-fallback chain into concrete
137:     `properties`/`strings` (`RenderTree::resolve_tokens`, reusing
138:     `pathland_core::tokens`).
139:   - **Tier-1 default tables** (light + dark) in `host.rs`
140:     (`concrete_default_tables`) — concrete platform-appropriate fallbacks,
141:     **enriched with GTK-native theme colors** (`tokens.rs`:
142:     `StyleContext::lookup_color` of `@theme_*`/`@borders`/`@success_color`…)
143:     from the first widget's style context (headless → concrete fallback).
144:   - **Scheme detection** from the native GTK variant
145:     (`gtk::Settings` `prefer-dark` + `-dark` theme name); a notify handler
146:     calls `GtkRenderer::set_scheme`, which re-enriches native defaults and
147:     re-resolves + re-applies every token-referencing widget. Scheme is never
148:     carried by the protocol.
149:   - The generative `space.<N>` family resolves `space.base` × N.
150:   - Since GTK CSS has no custom properties, tokens resolve to **concrete**
151:     values (rgba/px/Pango) before the existing CSS-provider / text-style paths.
152: - **App-driven media (spec/MEDIA.md)**: a **`MEDIA_CONTROLLER`** node (the
153:   playback owner; layout-transparent, **no widget**) gets a hidden **GStreamer
154:   `playbin` pipeline**, keyed by the **controller id** — so a `VIDEO` surface
155:   appearing/disappearing (e.g. a `SIZE_THAT_FITS` swap) never restarts the
156:   stream. Driven by the controller's transport properties: `MEDIA_SOURCE` sets
157:   the source URI (re-created on change, resuming if the app was playing),
158:   `PLAYBACK_STATE` → pipeline `Playing`/`Paused`, `MEDIA_POSITION` → seek
159:   (**echo-guarded**: a write matching the position the renderer last REPORTED
160:   — the app's `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` echo — does not seek, even at network
161:   latency; spec/EVENTS.md Media), `MEDIA_VOLUME` → playbin volume, `MEDIA_MUTED`
162:   → playbin `mute`, `MEDIA_LOOP` → restart from 0 on EOS (still reporting
163:   `MEDIA_ENDED`). The seek is
164:   also **change-gated** (only a `MEDIA_POSITION` that changed since the last
165:   read is evaluated — the web client's delta semantics) so the retained command
166:   value, which stays fixed during playback, is never re-applied as a seek as the
167:   stream advances (which caused the position to skip back periodically). A changed
168:   target is also **debounced** (a one-shot ~80 ms main-context timer hands the
169:   LATEST target to the worker) so a drag flooding `MEDIA_POSITION` — or any
170:   continuous-seek app — never blocks the UI in GStreamer's FLUSH seek (coalesced
171:   to ~12/s, last position wins). Media events report back
172:   through the shared event sink/ring, **targeting the controller id**:
173:   `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` (the worker's ~30 Hz
174:   poll of `query_position` while playing reports whenever the position advanced
175:   at least ~33 ms — the ~30/s cadence the web client shares — suppressed briefly
176:   after a seek), `MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED` (the worker reports the duration once
177:   known / on change), `MEDIA_ENDED` and error → play-state-false from the worker
178:   polling the pipeline bus (`EOS`/`Error` messages). Playback is
179:   **GStreamer-direct** because GTK4's own media backend (`GtkMediaFile`) is
180:   compiled out of some builds (Homebrew's `gtk4` ships with
181:   `-Dmedia-gstreamer=disabled`); the app owns all playback state, the pipeline is
182:   the renderer's rendered output (the desktop analog of the web client's hidden
183:   media element).
184:   - **`AUDIO` is retired** (audio has no view — a controller plus the app's own
185:     control views); a **`VIDEO`** node is the only media surface (a container
186:     box; the video output is not a widget).
187:   - **`MEDIA_MUTED` / `MEDIA_LOOP` / `MEDIA_RATE`** are applied: mute + loop map
188:     straight onto the playbin, and rate is applied as a **rate-seeking seek** from
189:     the current position (GStreamer has no standalone rate setter). Every later
190:     seek re-applies the rate, so a `MEDIA_RATE` is not silently reset by a seek;
191:     rate ≤ 0 (reverse) is ignored — not a transport control Pathland models.
192:   - **Verified from the DSL**: a test builds the Rust DSL's `MediaController` +
193:     `attach()` + `Video` tree, emits it, and applies the frame to a `RenderTree` —
194:     asserting the non-visual `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` node carries `MEDIA_SOURCE` +
195:     `PLAYBACK_STATE`, the surface's `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID` points at it, and the
196:     controller maps to no widget (`WidgetKind::Invisible`). (A runnable demo
197:     section still needs a bundled asset — the Java GTK demo covers that path.)
198:   - **Media runs on a dedicated worker thread**: each media player owns a
199:     `pathland-media-<id>` thread that performs *every* GStreamer operation —
200:     state changes, FLUSH seeks, `query_position`, and the bus drain — so the GTK
201:     main thread never makes a blocking GStreamer call (the "UI stops responding
202:     some time into a song, audio keeps playing" class of bug). The main thread
203:     sends non-blocking control messages (`Play`/`Seek`/`Volume`/`Stop`) and a
204:     250 ms timer drains the worker's reports, applying the echo-guard/suppress
205:     logic (`should_report_time`, the post-seek suppression window set when the
206:     worker reports `SeekApplied`) before the sink sees them.
207: - **Asset root**: `pathland_gtk_set_asset_root(const char*)` sets a directory
208:   that web-style `/_pathland/...` media/image source paths resolve against
209:   (`/_pathland/assets/x` → `<root>/assets/x`), so desktop apps reference the same
210:   asset paths as the web demos. Applied to `IMAGE_SOURCE` and a controller's
211:   `MEDIA_SOURCE`.
212: - **C ABI for foreign hosts (`capi.rs`)**:
213:   - `pathland_gtk_run(host, on_event)` — pump a `pathland-view-native`
214:     `NativeHost`'s ring in-process.
215:   - `pathland_gtk_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` — pump a
216:     **`libpathland_core` ring borrowed in-process** (from
217:     `pathland_core_ring_mut`): the route for hosts that emit opcodes themselves
218:     (the Java DSL writes into the ring via `RingOpcodeSink` and the renderer
219:     pumps the same ring in place — zero-copy, no `pathland-view-native` host).
220:     `width`/`height` size the default window.
221:   - Both block until the GTK main loop exits and share `run_with_pump_sized`
222:     (the 420×220 default lives in `run_with_pump`).
223: - **Robustness fixes (exercised by the Java `SplitNavDemo`, which uses controls
224:   the Rust demo never did)**:
225:   - **Slider step**: GTK's `gtk_scale_new_with_range` asserts a non-zero step;
226:     the renderer previously passed `0.0` unconditionally (a `SLIDER` crashed the
227:     process). A `STEP_VALUE` of 0 ("continuous" in the DSL) now derives a small
228:     increment (`(max-min)/100`, min `0.001`).
229:   - **Lazy stacks**: `LAZY_VSTACK`/`LAZY_HSTACK` map to `WidgetKind::Stack`, but
230:     `stack_orientation` only accepted `VSTACK`/`HSTACK` — a lazy stack panicked
231:     at `stack_widget`. They now map to the same eager `GtkBox` orientations.
232:   - **Re-entrant control signals**: applying a frame borrows the pump
233:     zero-copy; a *programmatic* value change (e.g. `GtkScale::set_value`) fires
234:     the connected GTK signal synchronously and re-entered `emit`, double-borrowing
235:     the pump (`RefCell already borrowed`) and panicking. Such events are now
236:     **deferred to the idle pump** (`flush_pending` before each frame), which also
237:     prevents a control-echo loop when the host writes the same value back.
238: 
239: ## Not implemented / gaps
240: 
241: - **`SizeThatFits` (SIZE_THAT_FITS 0x17 / FIT_QUERY 0x1039 LIST / FIT_CHANGED 0x13) is
242:   NOT implemented in the GTK renderer (removed)** — a fit slot node is unmapped (no
243:   widget), `FIT_QUERY` is not decoded, and no `FIT_CHANGED` is reported. The protocol,
244:   core, Java DSL, Rust DSL/engine, web (SSR + DOM) and server-routing surfaces are
245:   implemented; GTK rendering is deferred because **GTK4 has no size-change
246:   notification** (the GTK3 `size-allocate` signal was removed; there is no CSS
247:   `@container` analog) — a future renderer would observe its own allocation via a
248:   frame-clock `add_tick_callback` (or a `GtkWidget` `allocate` override), derive the
249:   fit with `pathland_core::fit::fit_index`, and report `FIT_CHANGED` only on band
250:   crossings.
251: - **Layout contract (spec/LAYOUT.md)**: aligned — stacks apply the per-child
252:   rule on **both** axes (main axis: only `FILL`/greedy children stretch and
253:   leftover goes to them, everything else positioned at the start; cross axis:
254:   only `FILL`/greedy children stretch, otherwise positioned by `ALIGNMENT`
255:   defaulting to Leading), grid cells apply the same rule, and the greedy
256:   primitives (`DIVIDER` cross-axis, `SPACER` main-axis, `COLOR`/`SCROLLVIEW`
257:   both) fill by nature. The old composite-button main-axis hack was retired
258:   (superseded by the parent stack's rule). Conformance C1–C6 covered by the
259:   pure decision tests in `layout.rs`.
260: - **Per-child expansion is explicit** (`sync_stack_children`): each child's
261:   `hexpand`/`vexpand` is set from the same effective-`FILL` decision as its
262:   alignment, so a Hug main-axis child (`valign=Start`, `vexpand=false`) can
263:   never claim leftover — a `GtkBox` otherwise hands extra space to children
264:   left at GTK's default `Align::Fill`, which spread e.g. a library's rows
265:   vertically instead of pinning them to the leading edge (the trailing
266:   `SPACER` absorbs the leftover). This also makes `SPACER` cross-axis
267:   non-expanding.
268: - **Fill propagation (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §stack layout model)**: implemented —
269:   `effective_fill` in `layout.rs` resolves a Hug-sized stack/ZStack that
270:   contains a `FILL` child / `Spacer` / greedy primitive on an axis as `FILL` on
271:   that axis (SwiftUI/Compose parity), so it fills its parent's proposal.
272:   Covered by `fill_propagates_through_a_hug_stack`.
273: - **ZStack (spec/PRIMITIVES.md)**: implemented — every child is an overlay
274:   (later = on top) that keeps its own size unless effectively `FILL`, positioned
275:   by the ZStack `ALIGNMENT` on **both** axes (`sync_overlay_children`); the
276:   overlay hugs to its largest child; fill propagation applies. The old
277:   first-child-pinned-to-fill `GtkOverlay` main-child behavior is gone.
278: - **CONTENT_MARGINS vs PADDING precedence**: implemented — `CONTENT_MARGINS` is
279:   folded into the margins by `apply_padding` as the **lowest-precedence base**
280:   (per-edge `PADDING_*` > `PADDING` > `CONTENT_MARGINS`, spec PRIMITIVES.md §stack
281:   layout model) and no longer applied in `apply_style` (where it previously
282:   overrode the higher-precedence `PADDING`). Matches the HTML renderer.
283:   Covered by `content_margins_are_the_lowest_precedence_base`.
284: - **SPACING** (spec/PRIMITIVES.md): applied on stacks (`GtkBox` spacing,
285:   re-set every frame), on **grids** (`row_spacing`/`column_spacing` from
286:   `SPACING`, `sync_grid_children`), and on **composite-control bodies**
287:   (`sync_composite_children` reads the control node's `SPACING` — a control
288:   whose label flattened a stack, e.g. `Button.of(HStack, …)`, carries the
289:   stack's `SPACING`, and its body box reproduces the gap like the HTML
290:   renderer's `gap`). Covered by `spacing_clamps_and_rounds_for_any_node`.
291: - **`CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`**: implemented — applied in `apply_style` via
292:   `set_overflow(Overflow::Hidden)` (SwiftUI `.clipped()` parity, spec LAYOUT.md /
293:   PRIMITIVES.md: a Fixed box constrains layout but only clips when set).
294: - **Text layout (spec LAYOUT.md §content fitting)**: aligned — a Fixed `WIDTH`
295:   wraps the label within the box (`set_wrap` + `WordChar`); `LINE_LIMIT` clamps
296:   the line count (`set_lines`) and truncates with an ellipsis positioned by
297:   `TRUNCATION_MODE` (Tail default). `TRUNCATION_MODE` **alone** has no observable
298:   effect (`apply_text_style` no longer forces single-line). Renderer-owned
299:   fidelity: `ellipsize_from` maps Head/Middle/Tail → `EllipsizeMode::Start/
300:   Middle/End` — reliable for single-line labels, best-effort on a multi-line
301:   clamp.
302: - **Known GTK limitation**: a GTK Fixed box (`set_size_request`) is a **minimum**
303:   request — GTK has no max-size API, so a widget whose natural size exceeds its
304:   Fixed box (e.g. a stack wider than its box) is allocated its natural size
305:   rather than clipped to the box. Text wraps within its box (above) and
306:   `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` clips overflow; other content may still exceed a Fixed box.
307: - **Grid/ScrollView/Lazy layout (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §Grid / §ScrollView)**:
308:   grids set `row_spacing`/`column_spacing` from `SPACING`, per-cell alignment
309:   (`grid_cell_align`), and read the track counts from the `GRID_COLUMNS` /
310:   `GRID_ROWS` constructor properties (`grid_track` — columns for GRID/
311:   LAZY_VGRID, rows for LAZY_HGRID, cells column-major there). **`GRID_ROW`**
312:   (0x1D) rows are flattened via `grid_cells` — a row's cells attach at their
313:   computed (row, col); the row node itself maps to no widget (blank). `WIDTH`/
314:   `HEIGHT` on a grid are the universal pixel box, never a count. `SCROLLVIEW`
315:   renders its first (spec-pinned) content child with `Automatic`/`Automatic`
316:   scroll policy and greedy `Align::Fill`. **Gap: `SCROLL_AXIS` (0x0021) is not
317:   yet implemented** — the scroll view is treated as greedy on both axes, not
318:   axis-aware (scroll-axis greedy, cross-axis hug + fill propagation). **SCROLL** (the v/h Adjustments'
319:   `value_changed` → `Event::Scroll`) and **WHEEL** (`GtkEventControllerScroll`
320:   → `Event::Wheel`) are emitted for nodes with the listener bits (8/9).
321:   **Residuals**: `LAZY_*` realizes eagerly (spec-permitted), auto-fit grids
322:   collapse to a single track (spec-permitted; measurement is a follow-up), and
323:   runtime scroll emission needs a visual check (headless tests cover the
324:   wiring only). **`GRID_TRACKS` is not implemented** (web-only for now):
325:   `GtkGrid` has no per-column-width/fractional/adaptive API, so a grid carrying
326:   only a `GRID_TRACKS` spec falls back to auto-fit/single-track — use
327:   `GRID_COLUMNS`/`GRID_ROWS` on GTK.
328: - `SHAPE` `Path`/rounded rendering is an approximation (rectangle/circle fill).
329: - `MENU` renders a menu button without a popover item list.
330: - No `ACTION_ID`-only gating (events require `BINDING_ID`).
331: - Composite bodies attach to button-like controls only; other controls ignore
332:   children.
333: - `LAZY_*` renders eagerly (no GTK windowing).
334: - **Media**: a `VIDEO` node plays its audio through the shared GStreamer
335:   `playbin` machinery, but has no native video surface yet (a native `GtkVideo`
336:   widget additionally needs a GTK4 build with `media-gstreamer` enabled) — video
337:   rendering is a follow-up. Playback requires GStreamer with the mp3 decoding
338:   plugins installed (the brew `gstreamer` formula bundles them).
339: - The `AdwNavigationView` adapter does not (yet) reflect the `TRANSITION`
340:   (0x1031) hint into a native animation choice — libadwaita animates its
341:   standard push/pop; per-transition styling is a follow-up.
342: - **Duplicate same-route pushes collapse**: pages are keyed by the current
343:   route tag on top — a `push` to a route that already sits on top refreshes in
344:   place instead of stacking a second identical page (the app's back-stack is
345:   the source of truth for depth; the native stack is only its rendered cache).
346: - A **multi-step jump deeper in one frame** (the app emitting only the final
347:   destination) pushes a single page; intermediate pages are not fabricated.
348: 
349: ## Verified by
350: 
351: `cargo test -p pathland-render-gtk` — layout mapping, `widget_kind` (full
352: component map), container/composite kinds, string resolution, value type
353: mapping (headless; widget construction is exercised without a display), the
354: nav-slot detection + `nav_action` depth decision + `NAV_CHROME` mode
355: (`is_custom_chrome`), and design tokens: `DESIGN_TOKEN` property refs resolve
356: against concrete defaults, `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides + `dark.*` + scheme
357: change re-resolve, generative `space.N`, and the GTK-native default enrichment
358: (fallback path headless).

(End of file - total 358 lines)
